title: Chapter 13: The Needle Box
paragraphs: "Ah, what's the difference? Aren't they all the same?"

Chen Mobai's knowledge of array formations was limited to what he had learned in class. To him, the Azure Water Formation seemed only slightly more advanced than the examples taught in regular lessons, but nothing fundamentally different.
How could this be considered a completely different system?

"On Diyuan Star, all cultivation resources have been nationalized. The Soul Transformation Patriarch used a Supreme Artifact to condense and unify all the Spiritual Veins of the Thirty-Six Grotto-Heavens and Seventy-Two Blessed Lands."

"Therefore, on Diyuan Star, practically no one studies formations that require Array Flags to be embedded into Spiritual Veins. However, since this knowledge forms the foundation of formation studies, we still teach it as array formation teachers in high school."

"In reality, formations of Second-Tier Low-Grade or higher that require drawing power from Spiritual Veins have become relics of the past. The direction the Immortal Sect supports and that the Great Dao Academies and Palaces guide formation research toward is harnessing the power of natural phenomena—the sun, moon, and stars."
After Chan Si finished speaking, Chen Mobai finally understood: the Azure Water Formation, a formation that needed to be rooted in a water vein, was exceedingly rare throughout the Immortal Sect.

It wasn't that the formation itself was particularly difficult, but rather that obtaining permission from the Immortal Sect Ministry of Land and Natural Resources to draw spiritual energy from a vein within the sect's territory for deployment was nearly impossible.

"Perhaps the private tutor my mother hired was a cultivator who participated in opening up the sea territories," Chen Mobai offered, forcing an explanation. "That might explain their obsession with formations that require water veins."
Chan Si gave him a skeptical look but didn't press the matter further.
"Give me your phone number."
Chen Mobai hadn't expected Chan Si to suddenly ask for his number and was momentarily taken aback.
Chen Mobai was surprised by Chan Si's humility. Despite being a professor of array formations, she claimed to only have a rudimentary understanding of the subject.
"Thank you for your help, Teacher Chan," he said.
Afterward, he immediately took out his phone and added Chan Si as a friend.

Just as he was about to leave, he hesitated, feeling a bit awkward. He scanned the thirty pages ofDetailed Explanation of the Azure Water Formation—photos stored on his phone—into a text document and sent it to Chan Si, claiming it was reference material given to him by his private tutor.
"Mm, with this, I should be able to give you an answer within the next couple of days. After all, the essence of array formations remains constant despite their myriad variations."

Chan Si's eyes lit up when she saw the document Chen Mobai had sent. She immediately pulled out paper and a pen and began calculating and simulating the operation of the Azure Water Formation, seemingly determined to deduce its full mysteries through her own efforts first.
Seeing her engrossed in concentration, Chen Mobai didn't dare disturb her. He quietly backed out and closed the door behind him.

He had initially considered giving Chan Si the original copy ofDetailed Explanation of the Azure Water Formationfor reference. However, remembering that its origins might lie beyond the Immortal Sect's territory and that it could serve as evidence implicating him in a murder, he decided caution was paramount.
After careful consideration, Chen Mobai decided to scan the entire book into a document, word by word. After removing any traces that might reveal its origin, he would send it to Chan Si.
Leaving the office, Chen Mobai planned to head straight home.
Now that he possessed a Second-Tier Mid-Grade Spiritual Vein Treasure Land, he had little interest in the school's First-Tier Spiritual Energy Cultivation Chambers.
However, after a moment's reflection, he decided it was best to avoid drawing attention to himself.

Immortal Sect Fifth High School was a national institution, and most of its students came from ordinary families. Even geniuses like Song Zheng and Yan Bingxuan, who had already reached the Late-Stage of Qi Refinement, cherished their two hours of free cultivation time each afternoon.

It wasn't unheard of for students to forgo the school's Cultivation Chambers. Three students who had reached the Eighth Layer of Qi Refinement found the First-Tier peak-grade Spiritual Energy insufficient for their needs. Their parents had rented Second-Tier Low-Grade private Cultivation Chambers outside the school, allowing them to leave campus immediately after morning classes.
Therefore, if Chen Mobai stopped using the school's Cultivation Chambers, it would inevitably attract attention.

Qi Refinement cultivators were restricted to no more than eight hours of daily cultivation, as exceeding this limit would overwhelm their meridians and dantian. Chen Mobai had no intention of wasting his time here.
Thus, in the school's Cultivation Chamber, he retrieved the Flying Needle Sect disciple handbook that the brown-robed youth had dropped and began to study it.
The handbook was a slim twelve pages.

The first few pages provided a lengthy introduction to the sect's origins, tracing its lineage back to the Flying Sand Sect within the Ten Directions Hall. The sect's founder, having achieved Foundation Establishment but with no hope of reaching Golden Core Formation, eventually left the mountain gate.
The following two or three pages glorified this sect founder's arrival in the Eastern Barrens, recounting how he established a three-century legacy and earned widespread renown.
Following this were the standard rules common to all major sects: prohibitions against betraying one's master or ancestors, committing evil deeds, and other similar regulations.
None of this was particularly useful to Chen Mobai. Only the page detailing sect benefits gave him a basic understanding of how Spirit Stones were distributed.
Joining the Flying Needle Sect, in addition to sect responsibilities, naturally came with the annual distribution of Spirit Stones.

Early-Stage Qi Refinement disciples received five Spirit Stones per year, while Mid-Stage Qi Refinement disciples earned ten. Late-Stage Qi Refinement disciples saw their allocation increase to twenty Spirit Stones annually.

The brown-robed youth was a cultivator at the Sixth Layer of Qi Refinement, having reached the peak of the Mid-Stage. Ten Spirit Stones were hardly enough for his cultivation needs. He had likely colluded with the old man to open this Water Abode and earn extra income.
Little did he know that, fresh from the sect and before he could truly display his skills, the old man would betray him within the Water Abode, leading to his death.
The final page bore the youth's signature and the official seal of the Flying Needle Sect.
This sect manual was printed and distributed in the 6478th year of the First Era.
First Era?
That must be the local calendar of the Eastern Barrens!
By now, Chen Mobai had a growing sense of where the Water Abode was located.
Spirit Stones must be abundant in this place called the Eastern Barrens.
Once my cultivation advances sufficiently, I must leave the Water Abode and explore the mainland.
After finishing the Flying Needle Sect's disciple manual, Chen Mobai retrieved the Needle Case and gently opened it, eager to attempt refining the needles.

Twelve earth-toned Flying Needles lay neatly arranged within. He channeled Spiritual Power into them, causing each needle to rise. After exerting his full effort, he managed to bond ten of the needles with his Spiritual Power, causing them to slowly levitate.
Could one control all the Flying Needles at the Sixth Layer of Qi Refinement?
Chen Mobai pondered this. At his Fifth-Stage Qi Refinement, he could command ten needles. If fully refined, this would be an ideal number to wield.
However, having never wielded a Magic Tool before, he found his Spiritual Power nearly exhausted after just three minutes, causing all ten needles to plummet uncontrollably.
No wonder the brown-robed youth always fired them in volleys of three.

Recalling the brown-robed youth's spellcasting, Chen Mobai realized how drastically he had misjudged the situation. Even if someone at the Sixth Layer of Qi Refinement could levitate all twelve Flying Needles, true mastery—effortless, seamless control—likely required at least the Seventh Layer.

After meditating to replenish his Spiritual Power, he attempted to manipulate three needles again. Though he managed to sustain the effort for fifteen minutes, the earth-yellow needles moved stiffly, unresponsive to his commands.
If only there were a proper Refining Art to go with these...
